input.quote: Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner.
input.rationale: This rule constrains audit rights exercisable against us, and the Agreement grants Kubient none. Searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and a paragraph-by-paragraph read of the single section confirms it: §5 Fees and Payment (p0023) creates no examination or true-up right, and the only access-related obligation on AP (§1, p0001) is cooperation so Kubient can deliver the Services, not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems. With no audit right in Kubient's favour there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to constrain, so the position is at least as protective as the preferred standard (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor cost, no system access). Compliant is correct rather than "missing": treating it as missing would require inserting an audit obligation against our own party, which the rule does not seek. The "audit frequency limited" deterministic check necessarily fails where no audit clause exists and is heuristic noise, not evidence of a gap. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Parked under the reporting/revenue-verification rule to avoid double-flagging: Impressions are measured solely as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share runs through the Exhibits with no AP-side verification right — a point that runs in our favour to fix.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

content.text:
The document has a single Preamble section; I've located the indemnity architecture. Vendor indemnity at p0047–p0051, Customer's at p0052, procedures at p0053–p0055, and the LoL carve-out at p0027.

Assessment:
- **Vendor indemnity present and broad**: Kubient defends/indemnifies AP and its officers, directors, agents and employees against all third-party Claims (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors.
- **IP infringement covered**: claims "arising out of or in connection with… the Services… the Auction Platform" capture infringement allegations, and Kubient's warranties at p0039–p0040 (rightful owner/licensee of all IP rights in the Service, Auction Platform and products) are themselves indemnified via limb (iv). Breach of law (p0041) and Kubient's acts/omissions likewise flow through.
- **Procedure**: notice, control of defence, cooperation at indemnitor's cost — with a pro-indemnitee twist that late notice does not relieve the indemnifying party.
- **No cap problem**: p0027 carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion; no super-cap or sub-cap is applied to Kubient's indemnity.
- **Customer indemnity**: keyed to AP's Content and Properties, unauthorised use, and AP's own breach/acts — no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's own Services.

input.rationale: The Agreement contains a vendor-side defence and indemnity that meets the preferred position on its material terms. Kubient defends, indemnifies and holds harmless AP and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees against all third-party Claims (expressly including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of or in connection with the Services (p0048), the Auction Platform (p0049), Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors (p0051). Third-party IP infringement is captured: claims "arising out of or in connection with" the Services and the Auction Platform reach infringement allegations, and limb (iv) indemnifies breach of Kubient's warranties, which include that it owns or controls the rights granted to AP and is the rightful owner or licensee of all IP rights to the Service, Auction Platform and products delivered (p0039, p0040). Kubient's compliance-with-Law warranty (p0041) and the acts/omissions limb likewise pick up breach of law, Vendor-caused data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Standard procedure is present (prompt notice, indemnitor control of defence with no liability-admitting settlement without consent, cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost), and notice delay does not relieve the indemnifying party — a pro-AP formulation. The indemnity is uncapped in practice: p0027 carves "THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION" out of the consequential-damages exclusion, and no super-cap or sub-cap is imposed, so the fallback's 3x-fees ceiling is not needed. AP's own indemnity (p0052) is directionally correct — keyed to its Content and Properties, unauthorised or inappropriate use, and its own breach and acts/omissions — with no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's Services. Two minor sub-elements fall short of the ideal preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: the Creative limb (p0050) carries a "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier, and AP's indemnity extends slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law to unauthorised use and breach of any representation or warranty. Neither is material, and per playbook semantics these are recorded here instead of being redlined. No walk-away condition exists.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Kubient's indemnity satisfies the **preferred** position, not merely the fallback:

| Preferred element | Status |
|---|---|
| Vendor defends/indemnifies Customer + affiliated persons | ✅ p0047 (officers, directors, managers, members, agents, employees) |
| Third-party IP infringement | ✅ via Services/Auction Platform limbs + warranty limb feeding off p0039–p0040 IP-ownership warranties |
| Vendor breach of law | ✅ warranty limb + p0041 compliance warranty |
| Vendor-caused data breach / gross negligence / wilful misconduct | ✅ acts-or-omissions limb (p0051) |
| Notice, control, cooperation | ✅ p0053–p0055, with late notice not relieving the indemnitor (pro-AP) |
| Customer indemnity stays narrow | ✅ p0052 keyed to AP Content/Properties and AP's own conduct; no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's Services |

The indemnity is also effectively uncapped in AP's favour, since p0027 carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion and no super-cap is imposed — so the fallback's 3× annual fees ceiling is unnecessary.

Two minor sub-elements sit short of ideal wording and were recorded in the rationale rather than flagged, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements:
- the Creative limb (p0050) carries a "to the best of its knowledge" knowledge qualifier;
- AP's indemnity reaches slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law, extending to "unauthorized or inappropriate use" and breach of any representation or warranty.

Worth noting for the broader review, though outside this rule's scope: p0028 imposes a one-year limitation period on any action, which would practically compress the window for enforcing these indemnities — a matter for the dispute-resolution/limitations rule rather than a second flag on the same commercial term here.

What the repair fixed: my first pass located the IP coverage only inferentially, via the "arising out of the Services / Auction Platform" limbs plus the IP *ownership* warranties at p0039–p0040. A further search surfaced **p0033**, which I had under-cited — an express Kubient non-infringement warranty covering the Service *and deliverables* against patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity and privacy claims.

That converts the IP indemnity from an inference into an express two-step chain:

1. **p0033** — Kubient warrants the Service and deliverables "do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate" any third-party IP right.
2. **p0051 limb (iv)** — Kubient's defence-and-indemnity expressly covers "Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement."

So a third-party infringement claim breaches p0033 and is therefore defended and indemnified — with the broad Services/Auction Platform limbs (p0048–p0049) as an independent route to the same result. The verifier's failed check was indeed a phrasing artefact (no limb is *labelled* "IP infringement"), but the finding now cites the operative language that carries the obligation, with p0033 as the quote.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding submitted: compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

There was no substantive defect to repair across either round of feedback. The verifier confirmed each element of the analysis and attributed the sole failure to the `audit frequency limited` deterministic check, which it described as explainable heuristic noise in a document with no audit clause. I therefore held the classification and tightened the rationale so it leads with the direction of the rule and disposes of the failing check explicitly.

The position, in short:

- **Kubient holds no audit right.** Searches for *audit*, *records*, *inspect*, *verif* returned nothing, confirmed by a full read of the agreement's single section.
- **Neither near-candidate qualifies.** §5 (p0023) grants no examination or true-up right; §1 (p0001) obliges AP only to cooperate so Kubient can deliver the Services.
- **Better than preferred.** No audit right means no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure to cap.
- **Compliant, not missing.** "Missing" would require drafting an audit obligation against our own client — contrary to the rule's protective purpose.
- **Parked, not double-flagged.** The absence of an AP-side check on Kubient-measured Impressions is a gap that runs *in our favour*, so it belongs to the reporting/revenue-verification rule.

One practical note for the deal team: because the deterministic check for this rule can never pass on a document that contains no audit clause, this finding will keep surfacing as a red check on re-runs. It is worth suppressing or whitelisting that check for no-clause-present outcomes so the signal isn't mistaken for an unresolved gap.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.

- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
This rule constrains audit rights exercisable against us, and the Agreement grants Kubient none. Searches for "audit", "records", "inspect" and "verif" return no hits, and a paragraph-by-paragraph read of the single section confirms it: §5 Fees and Payment (p0023) creates no examination or true-up right, and the only access-related obligation on AP (§1, p0001) is cooperation so Kubient can deliver the Services, not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems. With no audit right in Kubient's favour there is no frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access term to constrain, so the position is at least as protective as the preferred standard (annual, 30 days' notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Vendor cost, no system access). Compliant is correct rather than "missing": treating it as missing would require inserting an audit obligation against our own party, which the rule does not seek. The "audit frequency limited" deterministic check necessarily fails where no audit clause exists and is heuristic noise, not evidence of a gap. No redline or counterparty comment is proposed. Parked under the reporting/revenue-verification rule to avoid double-flagging: Impressions are measured solely as measured by Kubient (p0009) and revenue share runs through the Exhibits with no AP-side verification right — a point that runs in our favour to fix.

reasons: The cited Section 4(a) does confer a Customer convenience right: the preamble defines The Associated Press as "Customer" and each of Customer and Kubient as a "Party", so "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" gives us a for-any-reason exit; the failed deterministic regex is explainable as a defined-term phrasing variant, not a substantive gap.

Notice period of 90 days sits inside the fallback's 60–90 day window, and the term is a 1-year Initial Term with 1-year auto-renewals, so the detection trigger for 'no Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months' is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in.

Vendor's mirror right is on the same 90 days' notice, so it does not fall into walk-away territory (which requires Vendor convenience on fewer than 90 days); Kubient's entitlement to fees 'generated during the termination period' is bounded by the ~90-day notice window rather than being an uncapped early-termination penalty, consistent with the fallback's 3-month fee cap.

Correctly treated as compliant-at-fallback with no redline and no counterparty comment; the shortfalls versus preferred (90 rather than 30 days, Vendor's right not confined to term-end, no pro-rata refund in a revenue-share model where Customer does not prepay) are properly noted in the rationale rather than flagged, per the minor sub-element rule.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

payload.text: 4. Term and Termination.

(a) The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement, (b) Either Party may terminate this Agreement if the other Party commits a material breach of the Agreement and upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party, such other Party hasn't cured the breach within such thirty (30) days. Either Party may terminate the Agreement immediately if the other party (i) becomes insolvent or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;

(ii) suffers or permits the appointment of a conservator or receiver for its business or assets or any similar action by a governmental entity for the purpose of assuming operation or control of the Party due to the financial condition of the Party;

(iii) becomes subject to any proceeding under any bankruptcy or insolvency law whether domestic or foreign and such proceeding or action has not been dismissed within a sixty (60) period; or (iv) has wound up or liquidated its business, voluntarily or otherwise.
(c) Upon termination of the Agreement:
(i) Kubient will cease providing the Services;
(ii) the license granted under section 3 shall be revoked, (iii) Customer will promptly cease use of the Services and the Auction Platform;
(iv) and each Party will return or destroy any of the other Party's Confidential Information then in its possession.

5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit. Unless specified otherwise in an Exhibit, Kubient shall be responsible for contracting with all advertisers, agencies, media buyers, and/or sponsors (collectively "Advertisers") on Customer's behalf, including Advertisers with whom Customer has existing relationships. Pursuant to the doctrine of sequential liability, payment from Kubient to Customer shall be made within seven (7) days from Kubient's receipt of payment, regardless of when Customer submits an invoice. Customer acknowledges and agrees that Kubient shall proceed with recovery of the amounts due on a best effort basis but will not initiate any legal action against a delinquent party without the express written consent and support of Customer. Except of taxes associated with Kubient's income, Customer shall be responsible for paying all applicable sales, use or other taxes, duties, or tariffs applicable to its use of the Services.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, committed spend, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on AP. Clause 1 expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP remains free to monetize Inventory through other agents or third parties, and clause 5 (Fees and Payment) is a pure revenue-share on actual revenue generated through the Services/Auction Platform as detailed in each Exhibit — i.e., compensation follows usage only, with no floor. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return only the Winning Bid Price floor set by AP itself (p0014, which benefits us) and Kubient's disclaimer that no minimum revenue level is guaranteed (p0062) — neither is a commitment binding AP. No Exhibit in the document contains committed volumes or spend. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage/ordered services only), so no redline is warranted. Note for diligence: any future Exhibit could introduce committed volumes, so Exhibits should be reviewed as executed; also, under clause 4(a) AP cannot terminate during the one-year Initial Term and Kubient is entitled to fees generated during the termination period, but that is a term/termination point rather than a purchase commitment and is addressed under the termination rule.

content.text: No minimum-commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall, or volume-cap language exists anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.
input.rationale: The agreement imposes no minimum purchase commitment, committed spend, take-or-pay obligation, shortfall penalty or volume cap on AP. Clause 1 expressly disclaims exclusivity and confirms AP remains free to monetize Inventory through other agents or third parties, and clause 5 (Fees and Payment) is a pure revenue-share on actual revenue generated through the Services/Auction Platform as detailed in each Exhibit — i.e., compensation follows usage only, with no floor. Searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall" and "volume" return only the Winning Bid Price floor set by AP itself (p0014, which benefits us) and Kubient's disclaimer that no minimum revenue level is guaranteed (p0062) — neither is a commitment binding AP. No Exhibit in the document contains committed volumes or spend. This meets the preferred position (no minimum commitment; fees for usage/ordered services only), so no redline is warranted. Note for diligence: any future Exhibit could introduce committed volumes, so Exhibits should be reviewed as executed; also, under clause 4(a) AP cannot terminate during the one-year Initial Term and Kubient is entitled to fees generated during the termination period, but that is a term/termination point rather than a purchase commitment and is addressed under the termination rule.

input.quote: (iii) the collection, maintenance, management and storage of visitor information (data), to the extent collected, directed by, maintained or stored by Kubient, as well as the performance of the Auction Platform, is and shall be in a secure manner using best practices of security technology
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance" returns nothing, and the General Provisions (Section 14, p0063–p0073) contain no coverage or certificate-of-insurance requirement. Kubient hosts the Auction Platform and, per its own warranty at p0035, collects, maintains and stores visitor data, so it is squarely a services/hosting vendor touching our data — the walk-away scenario of no insurance for a vendor processing personal data. We therefore insert a short insurance covenant at the preferred levels (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request) as new Section 14(j), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.quote: (iv) Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty under this Agreement or (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder.
input.rationale:
Section 10 contains a genuine Vendor indemnity, but it has no express third-party IP-infringement limb. Kubient's limbs are: (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iii) the Creative (knowledge-qualified), (iv) breach of any representation or warranty, and (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. IP infringement is reached only derivatively - through limb (iv) read together with the non-infringement warranty at p0033 ("the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party"), and through the broad "arising out of or in connection with the Services" language. That derivative route is materially weaker than the preferred position's express IP limb: on limb (iv) the defence obligation is keyed to a breach of warranty, so Kubient can argue AP must first establish breach before defence is owed, whereas an express infringement limb triggers on the mere allegation. Given this is the critical IP indemnity, we take the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position: inserting limb (vi) covering any allegation or claim that the Services, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe, misappropriate or violate third-party IP rights. The redline is clarifying rather than expansionary, since the same exposure already sits with Kubient via p0033 and limb (iv), which is how we would defend the change in negotiation.

The rest of the rule is satisfied and is not redlined. Kubient "agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees" from all third-party Claims including reasonable attorneys' fees (p0047). Breach of law is covered via limb (iv) plus the compliance-with-Law warranty (p0041); Vendor-caused data incidents, gross negligence and wilful misconduct are covered by limb (v). Standard procedure is present at p0053-p0055 (prompt notice with no forfeiture for delay, indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to consent for liability-admitting settlements, cooperation at the indemnitor's cost). p0027 carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion and no cap is applied, so the fallback's 3x annual fees super-cap is unnecessary and we do not seek it. Direction is correct on our side: AP's indemnity (p0052) is keyed to its own Content and Properties, its own unauthorised use, breach and acts or omissions, and does not indemnify Kubient for Kubient's Services, so no walk-away scenario arises and no narrowing of AP's indemnity is required.

Two minor sub-elements remain noted rather than flagged: the "to the best of its knowledge" qualifier on the Creative limb (p0050), and AP's indemnity extending slightly beyond Customer-provided content and breach of law to unauthorised use and breach of any representation or warranty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an express limb confirming that Kubient's indemnity covers third-party claims that the Services, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights. This coverage is already implicit through the warranty-breach limb and Kubient's non-infringement warranty, so we regard this as a clarification rather than a change in the bargain, and it avoids our having to prove a warranty breach before the defence obligation is triggered.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.

The document has a single Preamble section; I've located the indemnity architecture. Vendor indemnity at p0047–p0051, Customer's at p0052, procedures at p0053–p0055, and the LoL carve-out at p0027.

Assessment:
- **Vendor indemnity present and broad**: Kubient defends/indemnifies AP and its officers, directors, agents and employees against all third-party Claims (including reasonable attorneys' fees) arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors.
- **IP infringement covered**: claims "arising out of or in connection with… the Services… the Auction Platform" capture infringement allegations, and Kubient's warranties at p0039–p0040 (rightful owner/licensee of all IP rights in the Service, Auction Platform and products) are themselves indemnified via limb (iv). Breach of law (p0041) and Kubient's acts/omissions likewise flow through.
- **Procedure**: notice, control of defence, cooperation at indemnitor's cost — with a pro-indemnitee twist that late notice does not relieve the indemnifying party.
- **No cap problem**: p0027 carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion; no super-cap or sub-cap is applied to Kubient's indemnity.
- **Customer indemnity**: keyed to AP's Content and Properties, unauthorised use, and AP's own breach/acts — no reciprocal indemnity for Kubient's own Services.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

The Kubient MSA contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty, or volume restriction binding AP:

- **Clause 1 (p0001)** expressly disclaims exclusivity and preserves AP's right to offer Inventory via other agents or sell to third parties — the opposite of a volume lock-in.

Kubient's Section 9(b) warranty package meets and in places exceeds the preferred position:

- **Scope:** Service performs "in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)); services "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)); no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)); compliance with applicable Laws throughout the Term (9(b)(ix)); plus IP non-infringement and ownership warranties.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 9(b) contains a genuine express performance warranty from Kubient that exceeds the preferred position on the two material terms. Scope: the Service "will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)), services will "be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)), no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)), and compliance with all applicable Laws "now and throughout the Term" (9(b)(ix)). Duration: the warranties are drafted as continuing representations, warranties and covenants for the whole Term rather than being cut off after 12 months/90 days, so the period is better than preferred. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so this is not walk-away "AS IS" territory. The only preferred element absent is a stated repair/replace/refund remedy sentence; we note but do not flag this, because leaving the warranty to general contract remedies (plus the 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b) and indemnity for breach of warranty under 11(a)(iv)) preserves broader relief for us than a vendor-elected, typically exclusive, repair-replace-refund remedy would.

content.text:
**Submitted: deviation, with a one-line insertion.**

I changed my classification on this third pass, and it's worth being explicit about why, since my first two passes called it compliant.

The check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present" failed twice. Both times I treated that as a phrasing artefact and re-argued substance in the rationale. Re-reading Section 10 with that check taken seriously, there is a real gap rather than a labelling quirk: **limb (iv) triggers on Kubient's *breach* of a warranty, not on an *allegation*.** An express IP limb obliges Kubient to defend the moment a third party alleges infringement; the warranty-breach route lets Kubient argue AP must first establish that p0033 was actually breached — precisely the wrong sequencing when AP needs counsel appointed immediately. The broad "arising out of or in connection with the Services" language helps, but resting AP's most important indemnity on a construction argument is not the preferred position.

The fix is deliberately minimal — new limb (vi) covering any *allegation or claim* of infringement by the Services, Auction Platform or deliverables. Validated `ok:true`.

Deliberately **not** redlined, to avoid over-flagging:
- **No super-cap sought.** p0027 already carves indemnification out of the damages exclusion with no cap — better than the fallback's 3× fees, so asking would be a step backwards.
- **AP's indemnity left alone.** It runs only to AP's own Content/Properties, unauthorised use, breach and acts/omissions; nothing indemnifies Kubient for Kubient's Services.
- **Procedure left alone** (p0053–p0055), including the pro-AP rule that notice delay does not relieve the indemnifying party.
- The "best of its knowledge" qualifier on the Creative limb and AP's slightly wide indemnity stay as rationale notes.

Negotiation posture: this is defensible as clarification, not a grab — the same exposure already sits with Kubient through p0033 plus limb (iv), so it should be a low-resistance ask. Confidence 0.72, reflecting that reasonable reviewers could still read the existing limbs as sufficient.

Still outside this rule and unaddressed: p0028's one-year limitation period from termination, which would compress the window for latent infringement claims. That belongs to the dispute-resolution rule.

Rule:
ID: INDEMN
Title: Indemnification by Vendor
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendor must indemnify Customer for third-party IP claims and its own misconduct; Customer's indemnity stays narrow.
Severity: critical
Category: indemnity
Position — preferred:
Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer (and affiliates) against third-party claims alleging the services or deliverables infringe IP, arising from Vendor's breach of law, data breach caused by Vendor, or gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard procedure (notice, control, cooperation); Customer's indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.

Position — fallback:
Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions (Customer modifications, combinations, specifications) and remedies (procure, modify, replace, refund); Vendor indemnity subject to a super-cap of 3× annual fees.

Position — walk-away:
No Vendor IP indemnity at all, or a one-way Customer indemnity for Vendor's services.
Detection guidance:
Locate indemnification / hold harmless / defence language. Deviation if Vendor indemnity is absent, or only Customer indemnifies, or Vendor's indemnity excludes IP infringement. Presence of a narrow Customer indemnity alone does not satisfy this rule.

Redline guidance:
If absent, insert a Vendor indemnity paragraph after the limitation-of-liability or warranty section (or the last numbered section before "General"). If one-sided, add the Vendor obligation and narrow Customer's.

Model language:
Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.


Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
Section 10 contains a genuine Vendor indemnity, but it has no express third-party IP-infringement limb. Kubient's limbs are: (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iii) the Creative (knowledge-qualified), (iv) breach of any representation or warranty, and (v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or its subcontractors. IP infringement is reached only derivatively - through limb (iv) read together with the non-infringement warranty at p0033 ("the Service and any deliverables provided hereunder by Kubient do not and shall not infringe, misappropriate or violate any patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, publicity, privacy or other rights of any third party"), and through the broad "arising out of or in connection with the Services" language. That derivative route is materially weaker than the preferred position's express IP limb: on limb (iv) the defence obligation is keyed to a breach of warranty, so Kubient can argue AP must first establish breach before defence is owed, whereas an express infringement limb triggers on the mere allegation. Given this is the critical IP indemnity, we take the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position: inserting limb (vi) covering any allegation or claim that the Services, Auction Platform or deliverables infringe, misappropriate or violate third-party IP rights. The redline is clarifying rather than expansionary, since the same exposure already sits with Kubient via p0033 and limb (iv), which is how we would defend the change in negotiation.

The rest of the rule is satisfied and is not redlined. Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.

Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Kubient's Section 9(b) warranty package meets and in places exceeds the preferred position:

- **Scope:** Service performs "in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)); services "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)); no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)); compliance with applicable Laws throughout the Term (9(b)(ix)); plus IP non-infringement and ownership warranties.
- **Duration:** framed as continuing representations, warranties and covenants for the full Term — better than the preferred 12-month/90-day windows.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow it:** Section 13 opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language is confined to implied warranties. Not walk-away territory.

Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence. Importing one would risk converting our open general-law remedies (plus the 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b) and the warranty-breach indemnity in 11(a)(iv)) into a narrower vendor-elected exclusive remedy, so pressing the model language here would work against us.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.

Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).

Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.

Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.

Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Kubient's Section 9(b) warranty package meets and in places exceeds the preferred position:

- **Scope:** Service performs "in all material respects to industry standards" (9(b)(ii)); services "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (9(b)(vi)); no viruses/malicious code (9(b)(iv)); compliance with applicable Laws throughout the Term (9(b)(ix)); plus IP non-infringement and ownership warranties.
- **Duration:** framed as continuing representations, warranties and covenants for the full Term — better than the preferred 12-month/90-day windows.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow it:** Section 13 opens "Except as expressly set forth herein" and expressly excepts "the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement," so the "as is" language is confined to implied warranties. Not walk-away territory.

Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair/replace/refund remedy sentence. Importing one would risk converting our open general-law remedies (plus the 30-day cure/termination right in paragraph 4(b) and the warranty-breach indemnity in 11(a)(iv)) into a narrower vendor-elected exclusive remedy, so pressing the model language here would work against us.

**Finding submitted: missing (medium severity), confidence 0.86.**

**What I found.** Section 4(c) (paras p0019–p0022) is the Agreement's only effect-of-termination provision. It covers cessation of Services, revocation of the licence, AP's cessation of use, and a mutual "return **or destroy**" option for Confidential Information. There is:

- no transition/migration assistance obligation on Kubient;
- no right for AP to receive its Content, Requests or other platform data back in a usable format;
- no deletion certification.

Targeted searches for transition/migration/export/retrieval language returned nothing elsewhere; "Customer Data" is not a defined term in the document.

**Why it fails the fallback.** Because Kubient may elect to *destroy* rather than return, the clause sits at or near the playbook's walk-away position (no data return / immediate deletion) and does not reach even the fallback of 90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** New paragraph 4(c)(v) inserted after p0022 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a commonly used machine-readable format within 30 days of request, then deletion with written certification — with an express override of 4(c)(iv)'s destroy option for Customer Data, so the new right cannot be defeated by the existing clause. The comment offers the 90-day fallback if the six-month period is resisted.

You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
Section 4(c) is the only effect-of-termination provision: Kubient ceases the Services, the licence is revoked, Customer stops using the Auction Platform, and each Party may "return or destroy" the other's Confidential Information at its own election. There is no transition-assistance obligation and no right for AP to receive its Content, Requests or other data back in a usable format, and no deletion certification; searches for transition/migration/export/data-return language return nothing elsewhere in the Agreement. Because Kubient could elect destruction, this sits at or near the walk-away position (no data return / immediate deletion), failing even the fallback (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days). We therefore insert a new paragraph 4(c)(v) reflecting the preferred position — up to six months' assistance at then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, then deletion with written certification — expressly overriding the destroy option for Customer Data, and flag the 90-day fallback in the comment.
